newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma says capital normalising, no student unrest.
newsitem.headline: Burma says capital normalising, no student unrest.

text.p: Burma's military government said on Sunday the situation in the capital was normalising as there were no reports of fresh student unrest, but army tanks remained stationed at Rangoon city hall.

A spokesman told Reuters that the government request last week to opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi, to remain at her lakeside University Avenue home until the situation returned to normal, was still in force.
"Everything is quiet now. There is no student unrest. Most students have left Rangoon for their homes," he said.

About 2,000 students from the Yangon University and the Yangon Institute of Technology launched anti-government protests recently, and the government responded by closing institutions of higher learning in the capital. That sparked an exodus of students back to the provinces.
Most roads in the capital that were blocked after the protests were now open, witnesses said. But University Avenue, where Suu Kyi lives, remained closed.
The opposition leader has said she had no links with the student protestors and has expressed displeasure at the government restrictions.

An aide to Suu Kyi said on Sunday that the Nobel laureate and leader of the National League for Democracy (NLD) remained indoors on Sunday. NLD sources said she preferred to be at home rather than ask government permission to go out each time.

More than 860 students were held briefly after the protests early this month. The students were protesting police brutality and demanded greater political freedom and the right to form student unions on campuses.
The protests were the biggest seen in Rangoon since the pro-democracy uprisings of 1988 that the military crushed, leaving thousands dead or in jail.

Campus authorities and witnesses in northern Mandalay said two main universities there were closed, but the situation in the city was calm. Last week, students from the two universities staged a rally.

Diplomats have said that the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council's (SLORC) show of force, with the display of tanks and soldier-laden military trucks, had made it hard for the students to regroup.

The SLORC has been warned by Western powers to maintain Suu Kyi's personal safety and the European Union, the United States and United Nations have criticised it for its latest move to restrict student freedom in the country.
